summary:
Radar for 2026-10-30 (GLP-1 focus). The big new event is TRANSCEND-T2D-2. It's the first Phase 3 head-to-head trial of retatrutide, against semaglutide 2 mg in 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes. At 80 weeks, A1C fell 2.2% on both retatrutide doses versus 1.8% on semaglutide. Weight fell 19.5–20.9% versus 9.4%. Stopping because of side effects was 4.8–7.9% versus 2.7%. These are topline results, not yet peer-reviewed. First report: Lilly, Oct 28 ~10:45 GMT. ABC, Reuters, STAT and NY Post have covered it. News is near peak, but YouTube search for "retatrutide vs ozempic" should keep climbing for 1–2 weeks. Most explainer pages that rank now still say "no head-to-head trial exists", so they're out of date. Timing caveat: by today's 14:00 ET slot the result is about 55 h old. That's past the strict 48 h Lane C rule, and the comparator is semaglutide, not tirzepatide. Recommended use: the 13:00 retatrutide "new Phase 3 data" Short (proven lane: 268/202), plus a Lane C long-form only if the Editor accepts the 55 h age. Everything else this snapshot supports the Lane A queue with fresh hooks:
- Stopping (SURMOUNT-4, plus a new semaglutide persistence cohort, Oct 29).
- Protein (new Swiss loyalty-card study: protein and fibre buying rose at 5 months, then drifted back by 10 months).
- Bones and muscle, hair loss, and plateau (12-month real-world tirzepatide data, Oct 28).
For the 08:00 body-worry Shorts:
- The tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder scoping review (Oct 23; 11 participants with pancreatitis across 5 RCTs).
- A calm reply to the syndicated "Doctor warns of long-term side effects" segment now running on about 7 Sinclair local stations.
- The tirzepatide plus menopause hormone therapy data (the small benefit seen at 3 months didn't last).
Watch list: CagriSema FDA decision (Q4) and Novo's ObesityWeek data (Nov 14–17, Washington DC). Rejected: Forbes/Business Insider "where to buy tirzepatide online" and compounded content, and microdosing churn (Yahoo, Oct 29). Coverage, Medicare and earnings stories are banned lanes and were excluded.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg head-to-head: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 Phase 3 topline (1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin ± SGLT2; 80 weeks; A1C −2.2% both retatrutide doses vs −1.8%; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4%)
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide just beat Ozempic's top dose: what that does and doesn't mean for you.' Answer in line one: yes, more A1C lowering and about double the weight loss, in people with type 2 diabetes, over 80 weeks. Then the honest part: topline only, not peer-reviewed, not approved (Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027). GI side effects were similar to semaglutide, but more people stopped for side effects (4.8–7.9% vs 2.7%). Weight results in type 2 diabetes usually run lower than in trials without diabetes. Loop ending: 'and the trial that matters for most of you hasn't read out yet.' Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–10 days (YouTube search tail continues through ObesityWeek, Nov 14–17)
candidates.why_now: First Phase 3 head-to-head result for retatrutide, announced Oct 28. Covered by Reuters, STAT, ABC, NY Post, Fierce, BioSpace and local TV, but most ranking explainers still say 'no head-to-head trial exists'. Retatrutide 'new Phase 3 data' Shorts are our proven peaks (268, 202). Timing: about 55 h old at today's 14:00 ET, which is past the strict Lane C 48 h rule, and the comparator arm is semaglutide, not tirzepatide. Default to the 13:00 retatrutide Short and leave the long-form to the Editor's call.

evidence.signal: Primary topline release: greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of semaglutide 2 mg

n=1,298, baseline A1C 8.3%. GI side effects: diarrhea 28.3–32.7% vs 26.4%, nausea 21.2–23.8% vs 21.3%, vomiting 10.2–15.0% vs 13.2%. Stopped for side effects: 4.8% (9 mg) and 7.9% (12 mg) vs 2.7%. Full data to come at a future meeting and in a journal

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the new population-based semaglutide persistence cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29) and the Metabolites regain review (Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Open on: 'You've lost the weight. What happens if you stop?' First sentence answers it: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained a lot of the lost weight, and those who stayed on kept losing. New hook: the Oct 29 cohort suggests your early months on treatment are linked to whether you stay on it. Say plainly: don't stop or change your medicine on your own; plan any change with your prescriber. Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder: what a new scoping review found (Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23). 11 RCTs: pancreatitis in 11 participants across 5 trials (0.2–3.7%), gallstones in 73 participants (0.3–3.7%). Also a propensity-matched real-world comparison of tirzepatide, semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors (J Clin Med, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: 08:00 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short. 'Tirzepatide and your pancreas: how rare is it?' Trial rates are low, and reporting databases pick up more events, but those can't give true rates. End on the symptoms that warrant a call to your clinician right away (severe ongoing belly pain), in calm, non-scary framing. Absolute numbers only, with the unit 'participants'. Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men. Refreshed by the Med Sci (Basel) skin side-effects review
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (the L1 10-30 redo). The first sentence answers the title: hair shedding is reported more often on tirzepatide than placebo, is particularly associated with women, and is linked to rapid weight loss. No human studies show a direct effect on follicles. Cover what helps: protein, iron and other nutrient checks with a clinician, and patience. Never say 'most often' or 'it isn't the drug'. Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and menopause hormone therapy: does HT add to weight loss? Menopause Society 2026 real-world study of about 3,900 women (about 1,500 on tirzepatide). Tirzepatide plus HT: 6.6% vs 5.9% at 3 months, with no significant difference at later time points. The effect was larger with semaglutide

Honest answer: a small early difference that didn't last on tirzepatide; observational, so 'linked to', not 'causes'. HT decisions are for menopause symptoms with your clinician, not a weight tool. Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

evidence.signal: About 3,900 women. Tirzepatide plus HT showed modestly greater loss at 3 months (6.6% vs 5.9%) and no significant differences later
